parameter_interpretation: All ranges, rates, interventions, contract terms and investment probabilities are designer-controlled example settings.

contract_quotation.level_payment_formula: principal * monthly_rate / (1 - (1 + monthly_rate) ** (-term_months)); principal / term_months for zero rate
contract_quotation.rounding: Nearest integer cent, half up; final quoted payment clears the contract's remaining balance.
contract_quotation.fee_payment: Upfront from available cash; not capitalized.

tasks.name: Consumption plans under a changed monthly income
tasks.question_en: Choose the monthly discretionary-spending plan to use with the budget shown here.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Apply the assigned income path and chosen discretionary fraction; keep necessities and contract dues explicit.
execution_rules: Apply the stated income multiplier during months 1–12.
Use the selected discretionary fraction; keep essential spending and opening debt dues explicit.
Pay only from available cash and income; record unpaid obligations instead of allowing negative cash.

tasks.name: An unexpected household bill
tasks.question_en: Select a payment plan for the one-time bill shown in this budget.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Charge the stated bill once. Borrowed principal equals the positive funding gap under the chosen contract. Preserve unpaid needs when the cash-only option cannot fully pay.
execution_rules: Charge the one-time bill at month 0 exactly once.
Apply opening cash first. For B or C, disburse principal equal to the remaining positive bill gap once.
Use the quoted amortizing contract. Under A, retain any unpaid bill as a shortfall.

tasks.name: The size of an available credit draw
tasks.question_en: Choose how much of the stated credit line to draw for the planned expense.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Add the chosen principal once, apply a disclosed 12-month assigned contract, and separate spending financed now from the remaining cash buffer.
execution_rules: Disburse the selected principal once at month 0, never above the credit limit.
Fund the planned expense from available opening cash and the draw; retain excess cash as liquidity.
Keep any unpaid expense separate from contractual loan payments.

tasks.name: Repayment horizon and borrowing price
tasks.question_en: Select one of the fully specified contracts for the same requested principal.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Calculate rounded amortizing payments and total repayment from the displayed principal, term, annual rate and fee; do not use a market-price assumption.
execution_rules: Declining adds no new principal or payments.
Accepting disburses the stated principal once and activates only the selected quoted contract.
Treat regular payments and the rounding-adjusted final payment as contractual dues, not observed payments.

tasks.name: A liquid reserve and a risky allocation
tasks.question_en: Choose the share of available cash to move into the displayed investment, after the stated protected bills.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Debit only available liquid cash. Store the independently assigned gain/loss realization in execution state, outside the decision input; report cash and final assets separately.
execution_rules: Protect the stated bill amount before calculating investable cash.
Deduct the selected allocation only from available cash; keep the rest liquid.
A future executor may draw the stated gain/loss once at month 12. This dataset does not draw a realization or execute a ledger.

tasks.name: Competing debt payments
tasks.question_en: Choose how to distribute the stated repayment budget across the two disclosed debts.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Construct both debts from explicitly assigned contracts. Cap total payment at the given cash budget; track each unpaid due separately without creating negative cash.
execution_rules: Use the two assigned task debts and assigned cash pool for this allocation exercise.
Cap total cash payments at the displayed repayment budget and each debt payment at its current due.
For proportional allocation, round the lower-rate allocation down to cents and assign the remaining budget to the higher-rate debt, capped at its due. Record any unpaid due for each debt.

tasks.name: A revised repayment schedule
tasks.question_en: Choose the repayment schedule to follow after the disclosed change in cash flow.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Preserve outstanding principal, charge any stated fee once, and regenerate contractual dues after a selected extension or prepayment.
execution_rules: Use the assigned remaining contract for this schedule exercise.
Under an extension, charge the stated fee once from opening cash. If the fee cannot be paid, retain the current schedule; never capitalize the fee silently.
A partial prepayment uses half of cash above one protected income-month, capped at principal; requote only the remaining principal.

tasks.name: Cash from an asset or from refinancing
tasks.question_en: Choose a funding route for the dated payment, using the listed sale and refinancing terms.
tasks.ledger_mapping: Respect payment and settlement dates. Record sale proceeds or refinancing as distinct cash flows and preserve any unpaid bill.
execution_rules: The payment is due on day 3; opening cash is available from day 0.
Sale proceeds arrive only on the quoted settlement day. A day-7 sale cannot fund a day-3 payment.
Refinancing is disbursed on day 1 for the positive gap only. Record actual funding routes and any unpaid due separately.
